nodes.label: Architecture
nodes.detail: how the major components are structured and connected (judged on performance per unit area)
nodes.basis: keyword overlap with the problem statement + detected-domain affinity + editorial exploration priority (order only)
nodes.assumed_limitation: A fixed microarchitecture is chosen at design time, so it is optimal for the workload it was designed around and suboptimal for everything else.

nodes.label: Interconnect
nodes.detail: how components exchange information (judged on communication overhead)
nodes.basis: keyword overlap with the problem statement + detected-domain affinity + editorial exploration priority (order only)
nodes.assumed_limitation: Every additional participant increases the number of links that must be kept coherent, so coordination cost grows faster than the work added.

nodes.label: Scheduling
nodes.detail: how work is assigned to the available resources (judged on resource utilization)
nodes.basis: keyword overlap with the problem statement + detected-domain affinity + editorial exploration priority (order only)
nodes.assumed_limitation: A single centralized scheduler must gather global state before it can decide, so its decisions are always slightly stale under fast-changing loads.

nodes.label: Computing Model
nodes.detail: what kind of computation the system performs and how (judged on achievable operations per second)
nodes.basis: keyword overlap with the problem statement + detected-domain affinity + editorial exploration priority (order only)
nodes.assumed_limitation: The dominant computing model is uniform and synchronous, so it spends energy on operations whose result the application does not actually need.

subject: GPU

literature_overlap.statement: Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-004: Heterogeneity-Aware GPU Scheduling. Can capability-matched routing improve resource utilization for GPU made of deliberately non-uniform participants? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-012: Heterogeneity-Aware GPU Scheduling. Can capability-matched routing improve resource utilization for GPU made of deliberately non-uniform participants? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-016: Oscillator-Synchronized GPU Runtime Adaptation. Can emergent phase alignment replace an explicit global barrier to improve stability of achieved performance for GPU? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-015: Oscillator-Synchronized GPU Compute Model. Can emergent phase alignment replace an explicit global barrier to improve achievable operations per second for GPU? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-017: Heterogeneity-Aware GPU Runtime Adaptation. Can capability-matched routing improve stability of achieved performance for GPU made of deliberately non-uniform participants? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-013: Decentralized GPU Scheduling. Can decentralized coordination improve resource utilization for GPU in situations where a single centralized controller cannot observe the whole system quickly enough? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-019: Bistable GPU Data Representation. Can a non-volatile physical state improve information density per unit cost for GPU whose data representation state is currently refreshed continuously? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.

Investigate the primary engineering trade-off of: Direction DIR-014: Alternative-Substrate GPU Compute Model. Would moving the cost-dominant operation of GPU onto a different physical carrier improve achievable operations per second once interface overhead is included? by adjusting the dominant design parameter and measuring the impact on the domain metrics.
